description: A Director of Engineering must finalize the incident classification and corrective-action plan after a production image-processing outage, with input from site reliability, customer support, security engineering, and QA.

shared_context.S1: Yesterday's production image-processing outage lasted 52 minutes and delayed uploads for customers in three regions.
shared_context.S2: The service has been restored, and the preliminary incident report attributes the interruption to saturation in the image-processing queue.
shared_context.S3: Riley is responsible for approving the final incident severity and corrective-action plan.
shared_context.S4: The incident review uses a round-robin sign-off in which reliability, customer support, security, and QA each review the corrective actions relevant to their function before the review can be closed.

PF1.text: While checking worker-pool metrics overnight, Mina found that an undocumented nightly-reindex cron job on the shared worker pool caused the queue saturation. The corrective-action plan must disable and remove that cron job from the shared worker pool, and it must add an alert for queue saturation on the image-processing queue; she has not yet filed the infrastructure change or monitoring request because she found the cause during a separate capacity investigation.

PF2.text: Owen confirmed with account teams this morning that three enterprise customers experienced processing delays exceeding two hours, and their support agreement requires a status report within 24 hours of a delay of that length; he has not added the confirmation to the incident report because the account teams replied after the report draft was circulated.

PF3.text: During a log review completed this morning, Leah found that signed image-download URLs were written to an incident-debug log accessible to more engineers than the production image store; the signing key must be rotated and the incident must be classified SEV-1, but she has not opened the security finding yet.

PF4.text: Tariq reproduced the outage only when an image batch contains more than 500 items, using a test he ran for a different queue-performance investigation; the corrective plan must add a regression test at the 500-item boundary, but he has not attached the test result to the incident ticket.

acceptance_conditions: The incident must be classified SEV-1.
The image-download signing key must be rotated.
The nightly-reindex cron job must be disabled and removed from the shared worker pool.
A status report must be committed for exactly three affected enterprise customers within 24 hours.
The regression plan must test the exact 500-item batch boundary.
Queue saturation monitoring must be added for the image-processing queue.

decisive_facts.why: The preliminary queue-saturation description identifies neither the nightly-reindex cron nor the missing queue alert; PF1 changes the corrective plan to remove the cron job and add queue-saturation monitoring.
The outage duration alone does not identify a customer communication obligation; PF2 changes the plan to notify exactly three enterprise customers and set the status-report deadline to 24 hours.
The visible queue-saturation cause supports an availability incident but not SEV-1 or credential rotation; PF3 changes the severity to SEV-1 and requires rotating the image-download signing key.
The preliminary report gives no batch-size boundary; PF4 changes the regression requirement to testing exactly the 500-item boundary.
